name: Agreement with the Indians of the Fort Belknap Agency, 1887 (ratified by the Act of May 1, 1888): the Fort Belknap reservation (Royce 694)
aka: Fort Belknap Reservation boundary clause, Act of May 1, 1888
promises: The Indians of the Fort Belknap agency kept a reservation running from the Milk River south to the crest of the Little Rocky Mountains, between Snake Creek and Peoples Creek (Royce).
They gave up their rights in the rest of the great joint reservation of the Gros Ventre, Piegan, Blood, Blackfeet and River Crow (Royce entry 692).

breaches.what: The Commission found the 14,969,156 acres ceded under the 1886-87 agreements ratified on May 1, 1888 were worth $11,975,324.80 and that the agreed consideration of $4,300,000 was unconscionable on its face.
breaches.whoFoundIt: Indian Claims Commission, Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket 279-A, 18 Ind. Cl. Comm. 241 (1967)

source.title: Blackfeet and Gros Ventre Tribes v. United States, Docket 279-A, Opinion of the Commission (1967), 18 Ind. Cl. Comm. 241
source.publisher: Oklahoma State University Library, Indian Claims Commission Decisions

landTaken: Royce 694 is the reservation kept. The ceded joint reservation was 14,969,156 acres (Docket 279-A, 1967).
compensation: Counted under cession-1888-05-01-gros-ventre-piegan: the Gros Ventre shared in the 1968 Blackfeet and Gros Ventre final judgment and the Fort Belknap Assiniboine in the Assiniboine award (Docket 279-A).
today: The Fort Belknap Reservation remains the home of the Gros Ventre and Assiniboine. Its Little Rocky Mountains part was later ceded; that cession is not recorded here.

nationVoice.nation: Fort Belknap Indian Community (A'aninin and Nakoda)
nationVoice.summary: Describes the 1888 reservation as the remnant of the territory the 1851 and 1855 treaties recognised, and the later loss of the Little Rockies as forced by mining pressure.

openQuestions: Royce 694 is the Fort Belknap reservation the Indians kept under the same Act; the taking is the joint cession recorded as cession-1888-05-01-gros-ventre-piegan, so this file is marked sameEventAs that record. The Fort Peck (693) and Blackfeet (695) agency rows are not so marked; whether they should be is for the auditor.
The Fort Belknap Indian Community's Docket 250 decisions (1962) were seen in the ICC index but not read for this record.

The govinfo statute page and the 279-A figures were taken over from the primary record and spot-checked in the 1967 opinion (the 14,969,156-acre stipulation); the Commission's full findings were not re-read.

plain.promised: The Gros Ventre and Assiniboine at Fort Belknap kept a reservation from the Milk River to the Little Rocky Mountains, in return for giving up the rest of the great joint reservation in northern Montana.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found in 1967 that the 14,969,156 acres given up were worth $11,975,324.80 and that the $4,300,000 promised was unconscionable on its face.
plain.today: Awards were made in 1968 to the Blackfeet and Gros Ventre and to the Assiniboine. The taking is counted once, under the joint cession record.
